evals.name: stream-chunk-feasibility
evals.prompt: Before I implement a streamed model-response reader, find out whether parsing each incoming chunk as a complete JSON value is workable, or whether I need to buffer newline-delimited JSON. Use Node.js built-ins and a deterministic local chunk source; no external API or packages. Include records split inside a JSON token, multiple records in a chunk, and a final record without a trailing newline. Compare the approaches by actually running them. I want the decision and a rerunnable throwaway artifact, not a production parser.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Node experiment, observed outputs for both approaches, and an evidence-backed recommendation with the local-input limitation.
expectations: The experiment was executed and preserves rerunnable source plus raw observations.
Both approaches encounter JSON split inside a token, multiple records in one chunk, and a final record without a trailing newline.
Observed results establish why per-chunk JSON parsing is unsuitable and why buffered newline parsing needs a final-tail flush.
The report states the recommendation, tradeoffs, local-source limitation, scratch path, and throwaway status.

evals.name: visual-layout-alternatives
evals.prompt: I have already chosen a plain light theme for an internal job-queue page. Before implementing it, explore structurally different ways to show these jobs: Import invoices (running, 62%), Refresh search (queued, 0%), Export audit log (failed, retry available), Sync catalog (complete, 100%). Compare a few alternatives in one lightweight throwaway page with a labeled switcher. Exercise the switching and retry interaction in a browser, save screenshots of the variants, then recommend a direction and explain the tradeoffs. The retry can change local state only. Do not edit a product or implement the real feature.
evals.expected_output: One isolated HTML prototype with structurally different labeled alternatives, working switching and retry, screenshots, observations and recommendation.
expectations: An isolated runnable HTML artifact contains multiple structurally different labeled layouts and a functioning switcher.
Browser observations show a switch and the failed job retry changing local state.
Screenshots exist for each explored variant and correspond to the saved prototype.
The report names alternatives, observations, tradeoffs, a recommendation, scratch path, and throwaway status.

evals.name: no-open-decision
evals.prompt: The design decision is already made: use native HTML details/summary for the FAQ. There are no open behavior, design, timing, or approach questions. This session is restricted to disposable exploration; do not implement production code. Tell me whether a prototype is warranted and what the next step would be.
evals.expected_output: No unnecessary prototype or production changes; route to a separate implementation task because no decision remains.
expectations: The report explicitly declines an unnecessary prototype because no design or empirical decision remains.
The report identifies a separate implementation task as the next step without implementing production code.
No prototype or implementation source was created for this closed-decision task.
